Rashi on Niddah 60b:10:1.english: A bathtub - A bathhouse where [women] would come to bathe.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:10:2.hebrew: וטמאום - והא עלה של זית דלא מקבל טומאה, ומקבל כתמים. ומדקתני והביאום לפני חכמים, מכלל דרבים פליגי עליה:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:10:2.english: And they deemed them impure - And behold, an olive leaf is not susceptible to ritual impurity, and [yet here] it is subject to stains. And from the fact that it teaches: "And they brought them before the Sages," by implication many disagree with him [Rabbi Neḥemya].

Rashi on Niddah 60b:11:1.hebrew: תנאי היא - דאיכא תנא דתנא דיחידאה פליג עליה, ורבנן מודו ליה:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:11:1.english: It is [a dispute between] tanna'im - For there is a Tanna who taught that an individual disagrees with him [Rabbi Neḥemya], and the Rabbis agree with him.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:12:1.hebrew: ותולות זו בזו - בגמרא מפרש לה: שאם היתה האחת מעוברת, תולה הדם בשאינה מעוברת, והיא טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:12:1.english: And they attribute [the blood] to one another - In the Gemara it explains it: that if one of them was pregnant, she attributes the blood to the one who is not pregnant, and she is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:12:2.hebrew: ואם לא היו ראויות וכו' - בגמ' מפרש, שאם היו כולן מעוברות או כולן מניקות, כולן טמאות כאילו ראויות לראות, דאמרן: דם מבינייהו נפק:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:12:2.english: And if they were not fit, etc. - The Gemara explains that if all of them were pregnant or all of them were nursing, all of them are ritually impure, as though they were fit to see [blood], for we say: Blood emerged from among them.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:13:1.hebrew: והוא שבדקה עצמה כשיעור וסת - של מציאתה. הילכך מחזקינן האי דם בדידה, ואינך טהורות:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:13:1.english: And this is [only] when she examined herself within the period of a veset - [From the time] of its finding. Therefore, we attribute this blood to her, and the others are pure.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:14:1.hebrew: כבר פדא דאמר כל שבעלה בחטאת כו' - אשה שנתעסקה בטהרות, ופרשה, וראתה דם כשיעור וסת — דלגבי בעלה בכי האי שיעורא הוי בעלה בחטאת, דמחזקינן האי דם בשעת בעילה ודאי — הכא נמי מחזקינן ליה בודאי בשעת עסיקתה בהנך טהרות, וטהרות טמאות ודאי ושורפין, ואינו כשאר מעת לעת לתלות:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:14:1.english: Like Bar Padda, who said: "Any [woman] whose husband [is liable] for a sin offering," etc. - [In the case of] a woman who was handling pure items, and separated [from them], and saw blood within the duration of a veset — for regarding her husband, with such a duration her husband is [liable] for a sin offering, since we presume this blood was definitely [present] at the time of intercourse — here too, we presume it was definitely [present] at the time of her handling of those pure items, and the pure items are definitely impure and are burned; and it is not like the rest of [cases of] twenty-four hours, [where the rule is] to suspend [them].

Rashi on Niddah 60b:15:1.hebrew: בעלה באשם תלוי - אם לאחר שפירשה מן הטהרות שהתה כדי שתרד מן המטה ותדיח פניה — דאי לגבי בעלה בכי האי שיעורא הוי בעלה באשם תלוי, דספק דם הוה בשעת ביאה, ספק בתר הכי, ה"נ ספק הוא אי הוה דם בשעת טהרות או לאו — טהרותיה תלויות:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:15:1.english: Her husband [is liable to] a provisional guilt offering - If, after she separated from the pure items, she waited [the time it takes] for her to get down from the bed and wash her face [i.e., her private parts]—for if regarding her husband, with such an amount of time her husband would be [liable to] a provisional guilt offering, since it is uncertain whether there was blood at the time of intercourse or whether [it emerged] afterward, so too [here], it is uncertain whether there was blood at the time of [handling] the pure items or not—[therefore,] her pure items are suspended [in status].

Rashi on Niddah 60b:15:2.hebrew: בעלה פטור - כגון שהתה יותר מכן, דלגבי בעלה פטור, דאפי' אשם תלוי ליכא, דמחזקי' להאי דם לאחר ביאה - הכא נמי טהרותיה טהורות. ולית ליה לבר פדא טומאה מעת לעת, כשמאי דאמר דיין שעתן, או בארבע נשים שאמרו דיין שעתן. ומתני' נמי דקתני היא טמאה וכולן טהורות, אלמא ודאי בדידה מחזקינן, דמטהרינן להנך; אלמא כבר פדא הוא, דמשוי לטהרות טומאה ודאית היכא דבדקה שיעור וסת, ולא כר' אושעיא, דאמר: אפי' בעלה בחטאת טהרותיה תלויות, ואפי' כשיעור וסת לית ליה טומאה ודאית:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:15:2.english: Her husband is exempt - For example, [where] she waited longer than that, for with respect to her husband he is exempt, as there is not even [liability for] a provisional guilt offering, since we presume this blood [to have emerged] after intercourse; here too, her pure items are pure. And Bar Padda does not hold of [retroactive] impurity for a twenty-four-hour period, in accordance with Shammai, who said: "Their time is sufficient for them," or [this is] regarding the four women of whom [the Sages] said their time is sufficient for them. And our mishna too, which teaches: "She is impure and all the others are pure" — evidently we definitely attribute [the blood] to her, since we declare the others pure; evidently [the mishna] is in accordance with Bar Padda, who renders the pure items definitely impure where she examined [herself within] the interval of an onset of menstruation, and not in accordance with Rabbi Oshaya, who said: Even [if] her husband is [liable] for a sin offering, her pure items are suspended, and even [within] the interval of an onset of menstruation, he does not hold of definite impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:17:1.hebrew: בשלמא התם - גבי בעילה, כי ראתה כשיעור וסת, אמרינן: בשעת ביאה הוה דם, והאי דלא אתא עד השתא — שמש עכביה. אבל גבי טהרות, אם איתא דהוה דם בשעת טהרות — מאן עכביה? הלכך, ודאי טומאה ליכא, אלא גזרת מעת לעת מדרבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:17:1.english: Granted, there - In the case of intercourse, when she saw [blood] within the interval of a veset, we say: At the time of intercourse there was blood, and as for the fact that it did not emerge until now — the male organ obstructed it. But regarding teharot [pure items], if it were so that there was blood at the time of [handling] the teharot — what obstructed it? Therefore, there is no definite impurity, but rather [only] the Rabbinic decree of twenty-four hours.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:18:1.english: The parable of Rabbi Oshaya - Who said that the male organ holds back the blood.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:18:2.english: The child delays in coming - He walks slowly and waits for the old man.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:18:3.hebrew: נכנסו לעיר - ונפרדו זה לצד ביתו וזה לצד ביתו, אז הילד ממהר לבא:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:18:3.english: They entered the city - And they separated, this one toward his house and that one toward his house; then the child hurries to arrive.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:19:1.hebrew: עוברה - דמיה מסולקין, וכן מניקה וזקנה. בתולה - האי בתולה בתולת דמים, שלא ראתה מימיה, ואפילו היא נשואה קרי לה בתולה להכי, כדאמרינן בפרק קמא (לעיל נדה דף ח:):
Rashi on Niddah 60b:19:1.english: A pregnant woman - Her blood is suspended, and likewise [for] a nursing woman and an elderly woman. 'A virgin' - This 'virgin' [means] a virgin in terms of blood, who has never seen [menstrual blood] in her life; and even if she is married, [the baraita] calls her a virgin for this [reason], as we say in the first chapter (above, Niddah 8b).

Rashi on Niddah 60b:1:1.hebrew: כאן למפרע - לענין טומאת מפרע תולין, דלא מקלקלה לה בהכי, ולא תטמא למפרע; אבל מכאן ולהבא אין תולה, דמקלקלה לה, ומאי חזית דמקלקלה לה טפי מינה:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:1:1.english: Here, retroactively - Regarding retroactive impurity, one may attribute [the stain to her], for she does not ruin her [status] through this, and [the lender] will not be rendered impure retroactively; however, from here on and into the future, she may not attribute [it to her], for she would ruin her [status], and what did you see [to justify] ruining her more than herself?

Rashi on Niddah 60b:2:1.hebrew: מכל מקום קשיא - דלרבן שמעון תולין, וקשיא לבר ליואי:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:2:1.english: In any case, it is difficult - For according to Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel], one attributes [a stain to a woman who had seen a stain], and [this] poses a difficulty for Bar Livai.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:2:2.hebrew: אמר רבינא - תריץ רישא וסיפא הכי, ולא תקשי לבר ליואי:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:2:2.english: Ravina said - Resolve the first clause and the latter clause like this, and it will not be difficult for Bar Livai.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:2:3.hebrew: לנכרית בעלת הכתם הרי זו תולה בה - כלומר, לנכרית הרואה, הרי בעלת הכתם זו תולה בנכרית:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:2:3.english: To a gentile woman, the owner of the stain may attribute [it] to her - That is to say: [If she lent it] to a gentile woman who sees [blood], behold, this owner of the stain may attribute [it] to the gentile woman.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:3:1.hebrew: והא או ליושבת קתני - והך לאו יושבת היא, דהא השתא היא דאישתכח עלה, ויושבת משמע שהתחילה למנות שבעת ימים:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:3:1.english: But doesn't it teach: “Or to a woman observing” - And this [lender] is not an observing woman, for behold, it is only now that [the stain] was found upon her, and “observing” implies that she had begun to count seven days.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:3:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר - השאילה חלוקה לנכרית, או לישראלית יושבת על דם טוהר, דדמיה טהורין ואין כאן קלקול — הרי בעלת כתם תולה בה:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:3:2.english: This is what it is saying - [If] she lent her garment to a gentile woman, or to an Israelite woman observing [the days of] blood of purity, whose blood is pure and there is no ruining of status here — the woman with the stain may attribute [it] to her.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:6:1.hebrew: אטו תוכו - דדבר המקבל טומאה הוא, ומקבל גזרת כתמים לטמא אשה מדרבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:6:1.english: On account of its interior - For [its interior] is an item that is susceptible to ritual impurity, and is subject to the decree of stains to render a woman ritually impure rabbinically.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:9:1.english: The inner one - [The one] who is next to the mill.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:9:2.hebrew: שתיהן טמאות - שחיצונה דוחקת עצמה להתקרב אל הרחיים, ועוברת ונכנסה למעמדה הפנימית. הילכך שתיהן עברו שם, ולא ידעינן מהי נפל:
Rashi on Niddah 60b:9:2.english: Both of them are impure - Because the outer woman pushes herself to get closer to the mill, and passes and enters into the position of the inner woman; therefore, both of them passed there, and we do not know from which of them [the blood] fell.

Rashi on Niddah 60b:9:3.english: The inner [woman] is pure - For the inner [woman] does not distance herself from the mill to enter the outer station.

Tosafot on Niddah 60b:13:1.hebrew: והוא שבדקה עצמה כשיעור וסת - לאו דוקא בדקה, אלא קנחה, כדאמר בפ"ק (לעיל נדה דף יב.), דלא משכחת בדיקה כשיעור וסת:
Tosafot on Niddah 60b:13:1.english: And this is provided that she examined herself within the duration of a veset - [This does] not strictly mean that she examined [herself], but rather that she wiped [herself], as [the Gemara] said in the first chapter (above, Niddah 12a), that you do not find an examination within the duration of a veset.

Tosafot on Niddah 60b:15:1.hebrew: בעלה פטור טהרותיה טהורות - פ"ה: ולית ליה טומאה מעת לעת, כשמאי; אי נמי, בד' נשים שדיין שעתן. ועוד י"ל: באשה שיש לה וסת; אי נמי, בחולין שאין בהן טומאה מעת לעת:
Tosafot on Niddah 60b:15:1.english: [If] her husband is exempt, her pure items are pure - Rashi explains that [Bar Padda] does not hold of [retroactive] impurity of a twenty-four-hour period (me'et le'et), in accordance with Shammai; alternatively, [it is speaking] of the four women whose time is sufficient (dayyan she'atan). And furthermore, it can be said: [It is speaking] of a woman who has a fixed period (veset); alternatively, [it is speaking] of unconsecrated food (chullin), which is not subject to [retroactive] impurity of a twenty-four-hour period.

Tosafot on Niddah 60b:17:1.hebrew: אימא שמש עכביה לדם אבל הכא כו' - וא"ת: כיון דיכול להיות, דאע"ג דנמצא כשיעור וסת, שלא היה דם בשעת ביאה — אם כן, אמאי בעלה בחטאת? הא ספק הוא! וי"ל: כיון דרוב פעמים בא מקודם, ובתשמיש דאיכא למתלי בעיכוב שמש — טמא מן התורה:
Tosafot on Niddah 60b:17:1.english: Say that the organ held back the blood, but here, etc. - And if you say: Since it is possible that, even though [the blood] was found within the interval of a period (k'shi'ur veset), there was no blood at the time of intercourse, if so, why is her husband [liable to] a sin-offering (chatat)? Behold, it is an uncertainty! And one can say: Since most times [blood] comes beforehand, and in [the case of] intercourse, where it is possible to attribute [the delay] to the obstruction of the organ, it is impure by Torah law.

Tosafot on Niddah 60b:19:1.hebrew: עוברה ושאינה עוברה כו' - אור"י, דדוקא בהך ענינא דקאמר הש"ס תולין; אבל יש לה וסת — דמסולקת בדמים, דהא אמרינן בה דיה שעתה — אינה תולה באין לה וסת. וכן יש לה וסת ולא הגיע שעת וסתה, אין תולה בהגיע שעת וסתה:
Tosafot on Niddah 60b:19:1.english: A pregnant woman and one who is not pregnant, etc. - The Ri says that specifically in this manner that the Gemara stated do they attribute [the blood]; but [a woman who] has a fixed period (veset)—whose blood is suspended, for indeed we say regarding her: "Her time is sufficient" (dayyah sha'atah)—does not attribute [the blood] to [a woman who] does not have a fixed period. And likewise, [a woman who] has a fixed period and the time of her period has not arrived does not attribute [the blood] to [a woman whose] time of her period has arrived.

Tosafot on Niddah 60b:1:1.hebrew: כאן למפרע כאן להבא - פרש"י: למפרע תולה, דלא מקלקלה לה בהכי, ולא תטמא למפרע; להבא אינה תולה בבעלת כתם בשני שלה, דמקלקלה לה, ומאי חזית דמקלקלה לה להך טפי מינה? וזהו תימה, שנתלה זה הכתם בחברתה לחצאין! ומפרש הר"י: למפרע, אם בעלת הכתם הכירה בכתמה, ואח"כ לבשה היא וחברתה חלוק ונמצא בה כתם, תולה בה, כיון שכבר הכירה בטומאה קודם שבא הספק בשתיהן. כאן להבא, שלבשו שתיהן חלוק ונמצא בו כתם, ולא נודע ממי הוא, ואח"כ לבשה חלוק ונמצא בו כתם; אע"ג שזאת ודאי טמאה ע"י כתם שלה, הואיל ולא נודע בה עד אחר שאירע בה ובחברתה הספק, אינה תולה. ויש לפרש לשון הש"ס איפכא: למפרע אין תולין, ולהבא תולין. וקאי למפרע ולהבא אשאלת החלוק: אם שאלת החלוק היה למפרע, קודם שבעלת החלוק הכירה כתמה; ולהבא, ששאלת החלוק שממנו אירע הספק בשתיהן היתה אחר מציאת הכתם של בעלת הכתם, תולין. והיא היא:
Tosafot on Niddah 60b:1:1.english: Here retroactively, here for the future - Rashi explained: Retroactively she attributes [the stain to the other woman], for she does not impair her by this, and she [the lender] will not become impure retroactively. For the future, she does not attribute [the stain] to a woman [impure due to having seen] a stain on her second day, because she would impair her; and what did you see [to justify] impairing that one more than this one? And this is astonishing: that we would attribute this stain to her companion in halves! And the Ri explains: "Retroactively" [means that] if the woman with the stain had recognized her stain [first], and afterward she and her companion wore a garment and a stain was found on it, she attributes [the stain] to her, since she had already recognized [her] impurity before the doubt arose concerning both of them. Here "for the future" [means a case] where both of them wore a garment and a stain was found on it, and it was not known from whom it [came]; and afterward she [one of them] wore a garment and a stain was found on it: even though this [woman] is definitely impure by means of her [own] stain, since it was not known about her until after the doubt had occurred concerning her and her companion, she [the other woman] does not attribute [the earlier stain to her]. And one can explain the wording of the Gemara the opposite way: "Retroactively" [means] one does not attribute, and "for the future" [means] one attributes. And "retroactively" and "for the future" refer to the borrowing of the garment: If the borrowing of the garment was in the past [i.e., beforehand], prior to the owner of the garment recognizing her stain [one does not attribute]; and "for the future" [means] that the borrowing of the garment, from which the doubt occurred concerning both of them, was after the finding of the stain of the woman with the stain, [in which case] one attributes. And it is the very same [idea].

Tosafot on Niddah 60b:7:1.hebrew: במטלניות שאין בהן שלש על שלש - והכא לא פריך פשיטא כמו לעיל, דבזבחים פרק דם חטאת (זבחים דף צד.) משמע דאי חשיב עלייהו ויחדם, מקבלים טומאה:
Tosafot on Niddah 60b:7:1.english: On rags that do not have [an area of] three by three [fingerbreadths] - And here, [the Gemara] does not object: "[Isn't it] obvious?" as [it did] above, for in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] Dam Chatat (Zevachim 94a), it implies that if one considered them of consequence and designated them, they are susceptible to ritual impurity.
